blockers.title: Caller cancellation is only polled; queued removal and active retirement obligations are unmet
trace: Admit one active request and a second queued request with an AbortSignal.
Abort the queued signal with false while the active request remains held: no abort listener removes the ticket; it continues occupying queue/storage until pumped, session close, or root failure.

For an active signal aborted with 0, let a valid reply arrive before the request timeout. The code validates/commits usage, then throws signal.reason. reconciled=true and failurePresent=false bypass Worker.close.
execute rejects with raw 0 while the Worker remains owned and reusable until later root close. Session.close after that rejection has no active ticket to join.
blockers.required: Add tracked cancellation enrollment/removal with initial/recheck race handling and a retirement/settlement path for active abort. Preserve raw falsy reason, sibling-only queued cancellation, validated accounting once, and no unproved refunds; no universal hard-preemption claim.

blockers.title: Exact own-data validation is followed by unvalidated inherited iterator/map invocation
trace: An Array may have exactly the accepted own index/length descriptors and a prototype with a Symbol.iterator getter/function or map override. isProxy=false and Array.isArray=true still hold.
inspectInput uses for-of after array admission, consulting inherited iteration; copyInput calls borrowed pattern.map. validateRequest repeats for-of and copyReplyResult calls borrowed spans.map.
A map override can return the original array, so Object.freeze freezes caller-owned data and preserves aliases instead of taking the promised fragment snapshot.
These are source-defined dispatches, not an executed exploit or a promise to sandbox arbitrary host JavaScript.
blockers.required: Traverse admitted own indexed data without consulting borrowed iterator/map hooks; preserve cross-realm finite data rather than banning prototype identity. Revalidate/precharge the actual owned-copy boundary and never freeze caller-owned containers.

blockers.title: Owner.close does not settle or join its outstanding start/request promises
trace: Call the private exported owner.start(), then close before READY. close clears the startup timer; the exit listener suppresses fail while closing.
Neither close nor exit rejects/resolves the pending ready promise, so close may settle while start remains pending indefinitely.
With a pending request, close joins termination/exit but not the request promise; its timer can fail/reject later, after close completed.

Current Root.close waits for active.done before owner.close, avoiding this overlap on its normal path by waiting for request/start settlement. That avoidance is not an owner-level join guarantee and is insufficient for fixing active cancellation by promptly closing the Worker.
blockers.required: Close owner admission and settle/drain both startup and request waiters under explicit terminal reason/precedence, clear their timers, and join their settlement with Worker retirement. Do not introduce arbitrary late AbortError swallowing.

blockers.title: The payload formulas match, but parent metadata/traversal ownership is not completely charged
trace: Root initialization charges metadata(18): 19 units plus its 5-unit reservation token, total 24.

Under the ratified metadata-cell rule, root fields/container (16), EngineAccounting (5), TransportAccounting (7), bounds (3), limits (8), spent counters (8), queue/map containers (2), and the reservation token (5) total 54 logical units before any session. Map internals, Promise frames and Worker internals are excluded from this count.
Engine accounting/transport objects and their records are created before root metadata admission; their additional owned records do not have separate reservations.

Healthy validation allocates own-key arrays and descriptor records, inspection/validation return records and queue cells without a corresponding complete T census; usage snapshots likewise have no declared charge/exclusion.
Reflect.ownKeys also materializes all extra keys before the exact-length rejection. This is separate from the already-qualified exclusion of native structured-clone allocation before validation.
conflicts: D2 count every owned metadata/queue/session cell and distinct retention boundary
blockers.required: Supply an independently checkable full metadata/temporary/copy census and charge before the corresponding owned construction; retain cumulative spent versus reserved/live distinctions. If an exclusion is desired, request an explicit ROOT contract amendment rather than calling observable owned data VM frames. Payload U=47+4n+p+s and 479 alone do not certify the whole ledger.

qualifications.issue: Explicit stdout/stderr:true prevents default forwarding, but ownership is data/error callbacks only. close has no stream end/close barrier. An idle fatal stdout/unsolicited-frame event calls root.fail without scheduling immediate tracked retirement, so a live failed Worker can remain until root cleanup.
qualifications.needed: Demonstrate the exact pinned Node exit/stream lifetime guarantee or join stream settlement explicitly; exercise idle fatal output and delayed stream/error completion. Do not infer complete stdio cleanup merely from stdout/stderr:true or claim an actual leak was observed.

qualifications.issue: A Worker-close rejection may install an already-rejected Promise as root.#closing. Later root.close returns it instead of entering the normal barrier. Determine explicitly which remaining job/metadata ownership is quarantined and which independent cleanup is still attempted; preserve undefined cleanup rejection and primary precedence.
qualifications.needed: Whole-owner schedule with termination rejection, known versus unknown exit, concurrent root close and active.done. Do not convert retained metadata/quarantine itself into a claimed native leak; no branch has executed here.
